subject.title: [Bug]: Bootstrap files in agentDir are silently ignored — only workspace directory files are injected into system prompt

question: Should configured agentDir bootstrap-named files become an injected prompt source, or should agentDir remain state-only with warnings/docs when users put bootstrap files there?
rationale: agentDir stores auth/session/model state, while workspace is the documented prompt/file context boundary; changing that boundary affects security expectations and upgrade behavior beyond a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Warn and document state-only agentDir
options.body: Land the warning/doctor/docs approach so users learn to move AGENTS.md/SOUL.md into the per-agent workspace without making agentDir a prompt source.

options.title: Load explicit agentDir bootstrap files
options.body: Land an agentDir-loading PR only if maintainers want agentDir to become part of the prompt trust boundary and require upgrade/security tests for override and merge behavior.

options.title: Docs-only behavior clarification
options.body: Clarify the current workspace-only contract without runtime diagnostics, accepting that misplaced safety rules may still fail silently until users read the docs.

recommendation.title: Warn and document state-only agentDir
recommendation.body: Land the warning/doctor/docs approach so users learn to move AGENTS.md/SOUL.md into the per-agent workspace without making agentDir a prompt source.

likelyOwner.reason: The bootstrap resolver history and current blamed implementation point to steipete as the best available owner for this prompt-context boundary decision.
